cities: One store, in Chicago · independent shops, and its own site

craft_evidence.owned: YES - brand states "our mill in Winona, MN"; About page: 90,000 sq ft facility on the same Winona site since the early 1960s, designers and engineers "under the same roof". Brand news post (c. 2015, undated): "we often give tours of the factory" and names Bernhard Brenner as founder. Parent Miller Waste Mills (Winona) since 2023-24. All from the brand's own pages; no filing or tour read.
craft_evidence.makers: NONE - product pages say only "Made in Italy" (83 of 168 clothing styles) with no maker named
craft_evidence.mills: NONE - sourcing page names origins (Australia Merino, Nile Delta Giza cotton, Mongolian cashmere, Italian linen/spinning) but no mill
craft_evidence.madein: 210/210 (100%) of men's records state a country: 86 USA, 124 Italy. Clothing only (171): 85 USA, 86 Italy. USA: 52 of 53 knitwear, 20 of 21 polos/tees, 10 of 13 outerwear, 2 of 79 shirts, 1 of 3 trousers. Italy: 77 of 79 shirts, 3 outerwear, blazer, shorts, 2 trousers, 1 knitwear hoodie; also all 38 socks.
craft_evidence.heritage: dated and placed: founded 1960 by Bernhard Brenner (Knitcraft Corporation), Winona MN, named for the St. Croix River; timeline with dates
craft_evidence.process: YES - hand-linked seams, knit-in collar stay (late 1990s), seamless V-neck, proprietary knits, hand-cut/hand-sewn/hand-finished, boiled wool
craft_evidence.reasoning: Real owned making and a dated, placed history: a 90,000 sq ft knit mill and factory in Winona run by the brand since 1960, with documented techniques (hand-linked seams, knit-in collar stay, in-house proprietary knits). But it does not cover the whole range: 86 of 171 men's clothing styles, including 77 of 79 shirts, are made in Italy by unnamed makers, and no yarn or cloth mill is named. Knitwear alone argues for 5; the whole range argues for 4. Medium confidence.

ownership.owner: Miller Waste Mills (Winona, MN; family-run) - acquired 2023-24 per brand timeline
